_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Snow on the Blue Mountains this morning, and frost on the inside of my window. Winter’s here. This week, the tricks our own country plays: the Cascades that steal our rain, a cloud that sits still in a gale, and fog that freezes onto the fences.

replies.back: Oh, it’s moving plenty. The wind blows straight through it. You’ll see.

turns.them: After this one, you’re trained. Questions at the end, the last of the workbook.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions, the last of the training.
That’s the workbook done. You’re a forecaster, Harrow. I’ll stop calling you tenderfoot.
